rationale_overall: This week's pool skewed heavily toward noise: private-company milestones with no public ticker (SpaceX/Artemis 3 exclusivity loss, Blue Origin-adjacent commentary, Castelion hypersonic contract, OpenAI/SoftBank/Anthropic funding and chip deals), foreign/local-interest stories with no US-listed line (Japan nuclear-restart backlash, Shillong Times uranium mining protests, Indian drone/loitering-munition procurement, Korean HD KSOE SMR-vessel design, Pakistani satellite launch), pure keyword false-matches (Benson Boone 'Rocket Man' concert at Kennedy Space Center, 'Starship Troopers' video game update, '96.1 The Rocket' radio station, robotics student competitions, hydrogen-tank display at a 'Robotics Innovation Centre'), and non-actionable geopolitical/military headlines without an investable vehicle (Russian nuclear-capable missile test, Iranian missile-attack retrospective, Golden Dome interceptor test slated for 2028). The one item with a real ticker tie -- Google's quantum-computing breakthrough and its chip deal with Anthropic -- points at GOOGL, already held, so it confirms rather than changes the watchlist. A Yahoo piece flagging quantum-computing stocks as possibly due for a trim names no specific holding we own. Nothing surfaced a rising-wave vehicle with a near-term commercial catalyst strong enough to displace AAPL, GOOGL, NVDA, or SMR, and the run's rule requires any add to be paired with a remove, so no_changes is the disciplined call this week.
